subject: Chemistry
description: pH scale, acidic vs basic solutions, common indicators (litmus, methyl orange, phenolphthalein, universal indicator), titrations.

questions.explanation: pH SCALE typically ranges from 0 to 14 for AQUEOUS solutions at 25°C. KEY VALUES: pH < 7 = ACIDIC. pH = 7 = NEUTRAL (pure water). pH > 7 = BASIC/ALKALINE. DEFINITION: pH = −log₁₀[H⁺] (negative log of hydrogen-ion concentration in mol/L). EACH UNIT change in pH = 10× change in [H⁺]: pH 3 has 10× more H⁺ than pH 4. EXAMPLES — pH of common things: (1) Battery acid: 0. (2) Stomach acid (HCl): 1-2. (3) Lemon juice: 2. (4) Vinegar: 2.4. (5) Coffee: 5. (6) Milk: 6.5. (7) Pure water: 7. (8) Blood: 7.4 (tightly regulated). (9) Sea water: 8.1. (10) Baking soda: 9. (11) Soap: 10. (12) Bleach: 12-13. (13) Drain cleaner (NaOH): 14. EXTREMES: super-acidic 'magic acid' has pH < 0; super-basic NaOH solutions can have pH > 14 (rare). HISTORY: pH invented by SØREN SØRENSEN (Danish, 1909) — the 'p' stands for 'potens' (power) or 'potentia hydrogenii'. TEMPERATURE EFFECT: pH of pure water is 7 only at 25°C; at higher T, pure water has lower pH (still neutral). PYQ FREQUENCY: pH range is a NEET, NCERT-driven SSC 1-mark guarantee.

questions.explanation: LITMUS — natural pH indicator extracted from LICHENS (e.g., Roccella tinctoria). PROPERTY: RED LITMUS turns BLUE in BASIC solutions (pH > 7); BLUE LITMUS turns RED in ACIDIC solutions (pH < 7). NEUTRAL (pH = 7) — both colours stay unchanged. MNEMONIC: 'Acid Reds, Base Blues' (or 'BB-AR' = base-blue, acid-red). LIMITATION: litmus is APPROXIMATE — only indicates above/below pH 7 (transition is gradual). MORE PRECISE INDICATORS: (1) METHYL ORANGE — RED in acid (pH < 3.1), YELLOW in base (pH > 4.4); transition pH ~3.7 (good for STRONG-acid titrations). (2) PHENOLPHTHALEIN — COLOURLESS in acid (pH < 8.2), PINK/MAGENTA in base (pH > 10); good for STRONG-base titrations. (3) UNIVERSAL INDICATOR — mixture of multiple dyes, gives a SPECTRUM of colours: RED (pH 1-3), ORANGE (4), YELLOW (5-6), GREEN (7), BLUE (8-9), VIOLET (10-14). NATURAL pH INDICATORS: red cabbage juice, turmeric, rose petals, hibiscus. PYQ FREQUENCY: litmus colour change is a NCERT Class 7-10 staple, tested in CGL, RRB GA 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: PHENOLPHTHALEIN indicator turns PINK in solutions with pH approximately:
questions.explanation: PHENOLPHTHALEIN — colourless in acid/neutral, PINK/MAGENTA in BASIC solutions. TRANSITION RANGE: colourless below pH 8.2, fully pink above pH 10.0; in between (8.2-10.0), pale pink. CHEMISTRY: phenolphthalein is a WEAK ACID; in basic solution, it ionizes and the conjugate base form is pink (extended π-conjugation absorbs in green spectrum, looks pink). USES: (1) ACID-BASE TITRATION — common indicator for STRONG BASE + WEAK ACID titrations. (2) MASONRY/CONCRETE testing — used to detect carbonation depth in concrete (pink = uncarbonated, alkaline; colourless = carbonated, neutral). (3) Forensic — historically used in laxatives (until banned in many countries due to potential carcinogenicity, ~1990s). (4) FORENSIC chemistry — Kastle-Meyer test for blood (phenolphthalein-based). KEY POINT: phenolphthalein is a 'one-way' indicator for BASIC range; doesn't show transitions in acidic range. LIMITATIONS: doesn't show concentration of acid/base; only above/below threshold. PYQ FREQUENCY: phenolphthalein in Class 10 NCERT — CGL, NEET, IBPS GA tested 1× per cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests indicator-pH-colour mapping memorization.

questions.stem: Pure water at 25°C has [H⁺] = 10⁻⁷ M. Its pH is:
questions.explanation: pH = −log₁₀[H⁺] = −log₁₀(10⁻⁷) = −(−7) = 7. So pH 7 = NEUTRAL. KEY INSIGHTS: (1) PURE WATER autoionizes: 2H₂O ⇌ H₃O⁺ + OH⁻. Equilibrium constant Kw = [H⁺][OH⁻] = 10⁻¹⁴ at 25°C. (2) For NEUTRAL water: [H⁺] = [OH⁻] = 10⁻⁷ M. (3) pH + pOH = 14 (always at 25°C). (4) ACIDIC: [H⁺] > 10⁻⁷ → pH < 7. BASIC: [H⁺] < 10⁻⁷ → pH > 7. PRACTICE PROBLEMS: (a) [H⁺] = 0.001 M → pH = 3 (acidic). (b) [H⁺] = 10⁻¹⁰ M → pH = 10 (basic). (c) pH = 5 → [H⁺] = 10⁻⁵ M; [OH⁻] = 10⁻⁹ M (10,000× less than [H⁺]). RAINWATER: pH ~5.6 due to dissolved CO₂ forming carbonic acid (NORMAL acid rain). 'ACID RAIN' (pollution-driven) has pH < 5.0 due to SO₂ + NOx → H₂SO₄ + HNO₃. ACID RAIN damage: corrodes Taj Mahal (Yamuna pollution) — landmark 1990s issue. PYQ FREQUENCY: pH calculations are NEET, JEE-Main, NCERT-driven SSC top MCQ — 1-2× per paper.

questions.stem: The NORMAL pH of HUMAN BLOOD is approximately:
questions.explanation: BLOOD pH is tightly regulated at 7.35 to 7.45 (slightly BASIC). Deviations are LIFE-THREATENING: pH < 7.35 = ACIDOSIS (can cause coma, death); pH > 7.45 = ALKALOSIS (muscle spasms, seizures). REGULATION via THREE BUFFER SYSTEMS: (1) BICARBONATE BUFFER (most important): H₂CO₃ ⇌ H⁺ + HCO₃⁻ — handles ~75% of pH regulation. (2) PHOSPHATE BUFFER. (3) PROTEIN BUFFER (hemoglobin, plasma proteins). FAST RESPONSE: lungs adjust CO₂ exhalation rate (acid = more CO₂ exhaled). SLOW RESPONSE: kidneys adjust HCO₃⁻ retention/excretion. KEY pH VALUES IN HUMAN BODY: (a) Stomach acid (HCl): 1.5-3.5. (b) Saliva: 6.5-7.5. (c) Blood: 7.35-7.45. (d) Pancreatic juice: 8.0-8.5. (e) Bile: 7.6-8.6. (f) Urine: 5.0-8.0 (variable). DISEASES: DIABETIC KETOACIDOSIS — pH drops below 7.35 due to ketone body production; medical emergency. RESPIRATORY ACIDOSIS — CO₂ retention in COPD/asthma. RESPIRATORY ALKALOSIS — hyperventilation (panic attacks). PYQ FREQUENCY: blood pH appears in NEET, NCERT Class 11 biology, CGL biology section.

questions.stem: Antacid tablets (e.g., milk of magnesia) work by:
questions.explanation: ANTACIDS contain BASIC compounds that NEUTRALIZE excess HCl in the stomach, raising pH (relieving heartburn/acidity). COMMON ACTIVE INGREDIENTS: (1) MAGNESIUM HYDROXIDE — Mg(OH)₂ — milk of magnesia. (2) ALUMINIUM HYDROXIDE — Al(OH)₃ (often combined with Mg). (3) CALCIUM CARBONATE — CaCO₃ (Tums). (4) SODIUM BICARBONATE — NaHCO₃ (Eno, Alka-Seltzer). REACTIONS: (a) Mg(OH)₂ + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + 2H₂O. (b) NaHCO₃ + HCl → NaCl + H₂O + CO₂↑ (the 'fizz'). NORMAL STOMACH pH: 1.5-3.5 (very acidic, kills bacteria, denatures proteins for digestion). HYPERACIDITY: too much HCl → heartburn, GERD, ulcers. CHRONIC TREATMENT: PROTON PUMP INHIBITORS (PPIs) like omeprazole REDUCE acid production at source — more effective for chronic conditions. INDIA — POPULAR ANTACID BRANDS: Eno, Digene, Pudin Hara, Gelusil. SAFETY: long-term antacid use can cause magnesium imbalance (diarrhea), aluminum accumulation (rare). NCERT CLASS 10: antacid mechanism is a chapter staple. PYQ FREQUENCY: NEET, NCERT-driven SSC chemistry MCQ — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: If a solution has [H⁺] = 10⁻³ M, the [OH⁻] concentration in the same solution at 25°C is:
questions.explanation: Apply WATER ION-PRODUCT: Kw = [H⁺] × [OH⁻] = 10⁻¹⁴ at 25°C. Given [H⁺] = 10⁻³, so [OH⁻] = 10⁻¹⁴ / 10⁻³ = 10⁻¹¹ M. INTERPRETATION: the solution is ACIDIC (pH = 3); H⁺ ions outnumber OH⁻ by 10⁸ (hundred million times). KEY RELATIONSHIPS at 25°C: (1) Kw = 10⁻¹⁴. (2) pH + pOH = 14. (3) Pure water: [H⁺] = [OH⁻] = 10⁻⁷; pH = pOH = 7. PRACTICE PROBLEMS: [H⁺] = 0.01 M (pH 2) → [OH⁻] = 10⁻¹² M (pOH 12); [H⁺] = 10⁻⁹ M (pH 9) → [OH⁻] = 10⁻⁵ M (pOH 5). TEMPERATURE EFFECT: Kw increases with temperature — at 100°C, Kw ≈ 10⁻¹². So pure water at 100°C has pH ≈ 6 — STILL neutral, just lower pH due to higher autoionization. RECONCILE: 'neutral' means [H⁺] = [OH⁻], not [H⁺] = 10⁻⁷. INDUSTRIAL: pH control in waste-water treatment, chemical reactors, brewing — all rely on Kw relationships. PYQ FREQUENCY: pH-pOH-Kw calculations in JEE-Main, NEET 2-3× per paper. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests log-arithmetic discipline.
